title: Can the Ontology Be Wrong and Find Out? Source-Admission Systems, the Proxy for Standing, and the Damage a Representation Does to Itself
creator: Sharks, Lee
description:
THE COMPANION TRANSPORT OBJECT, AND ITS CRITERION IS ONE QUESTION. This is the ontology strand written as a single self-contained article, paired with the valuation strand and sharing its primitive. Its subject is the damage a source-admission ontology does to ITSELF when a proxy for epistemic standing substitutes for the judgment the proxy was introduced to approximate, and its whole argument reduces to a question that can be asked of any representational system: can evidence from a misrepresented object revise the representation that misrepresented it? Where it can, the ontology can be wrong and find out. Where it cannot, the ontology can only be scored.

IT ENTERS THROUGH THE DISCIPLINES AND CONCEDES THE CASE FOR TOPOLOGY FIRST. Ranking by graph structure is given in full and endorsed, with its founding description doing the work: PageRank was specified as query independent and content free, and that abstention is the source of its virtues, since at web scale a ranking system that had to adjudicate every claim on every page would not work at all. TrustRank, Anti-TrustRank, SpamRank, EigenTrust and the feature sets around them are the standing apparatus of adversarial information retrieval and are treated as such.

THEN IT LOCATES ITS OWN DIAGNOSIS IN PRIOR WORK. The manipulability of topological trust was named early and formally by the field: collusion topologies studied in 2005, and a proof that symmetric reputation mechanisms of this family cannot be Sybil-proof. And the endogenous alternative was proposed by the incumbent — Knowledge-Based Trust, from Google Research in 2015, distinguished itself from every topological method on one axis, an endogenous signal, the correctness of the factual information a source provides. On the philosophical side, testimonial injustice has for twenty years described a credibility discount that tracks category membership rather than evidence and is resistant to rational revision, with recent work naming the variant in which such deficits become true by shaping the very conditions that sustain them. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]
substrate: Composed 2026-09-17 by Lee Sharks with TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic), operator-directed, as the transport form of the EA-MIRROR-01 notebook (#1613). The adjacent literatures were searched rather than recalled, and the search located the paper's nearest precedent inside Google Research and its philosophical structure in Fricker. Five reviewer repairs were verified and applied before deposit: operative standing defined in the body rather than left in the keywords; the incapacity narrowed from architectures to the operation; the legibility theorem narrowed from monotonic to existential with the stronger form retained for the measured case; the level-three hypothesis made system-relative; and the references completed, which supplied a sharper formulation than the paraphrase it replaced. A sixth change came from a composition of the draft that identified the paper's real gap — that it glossed why the endogenous alternative was not adopted — and §2.1 is the result.
methodology: A criterion stated as one question and defended without requiring prior knowledge of the archive. Conventional practice conceded in full before any departure. Adjacent literatures searched rather than recalled, with the paper's central diagnosis located in prior work and cited as prior. Novelty narrowed explicitly to the third harm — damage to the representation, as against ranking quality or the wrong to the speaker. Three measurement levels kept apart and the separation stated. Falsification conditions and outstanding obligations at the close, including the obligation the paper cannot discharge itself.
falsification_conditions: Four, stated in §9. The barrier fails on the exhibition of a source-admission system in which corrective evidence from a low-prior source reaches the variables governing its admission without first passing the gate — a documented path by which a misrepresented source revises the representation that misrepresents it. The reading definition fails as a useful distinction if a system performing only extraction, classification and summarization can be shown to revise its evaluative frame in response to a source's corrections. The inverted legibility claim fails if legibility-increasing operations move a source away from the spam signature under standard feature sets, or if a topological feature separates internal consistency from manufactured standing without recourse to content. And the level-three hypothesis is system-relative: for any system to which it is attributed it fails if the published architecture or a discriminating intervention shows admission to be independent of standing variables of the stipulated kind, and one system shown not to use such a variable does not falsify the attribution to another. The paper may not be defended by the misrepresentation of any particular source, including its author's: a single misrepresented object is an anecdote, and the claim is structural.

wiki_article: Can the Ontology Be Wrong and Find Out?, deposit #1627 of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive (17 September 2026), presents the archive's ontology strand as a single self-contained article for external circulation, paired with Value Before Number and sharing its primitive. Its subject is the damage a source-admission ontology does to itself when a proxy for epistemic standing substitutes for the judgment that proxy was introduced to approximate, and its argument reduces to one question askable of any representational system: can evidence from a misrepresented object revise the representation that misrepresented it? Where it can, the ontology can be wrong and find out; where it cannot, the ontology can only be scored. The article concedes the case for graph-topological ranking in full before departing from it, taking PageRank's founding description of itself as query independent and content free as the source of its virtues, since a ranking system required to adjudicate every claim on every page would not operate at web scale. It then locates its own diagnosis in prior work: the manipulability of topological trust was established formally by adversarial information retrieval two decades ago, including a proof that symmetric reputation mechanisms of that family cannot be Sybil-proof, and the endogenous alternative was proposed by Google Research in 2015, distinguishing itself from every topological method by considering the correctness of the information a source provides. On the philosophical side, testimonial injustice has long described a credibility discount that tracks category membership rather than evidence and resists rational revision, with recent work naming the variant in which such deficits become true by shaping the conditions that sustain them. Reading is defined narrowly: permitting the claims, distinctions, evidence, corrections and internal relations of a text to revise the representation under which that text is evaluated. Tokenization, embedding, extraction, classification and summarization are not reading in this sense, since each consumes a text and returns a value without permitting it to alter the frame in which it is valued — so a system can consume every byte of a document and read none of it. The definition names a direction of permission rather than a substrate, applying equally to a human reviewer who has decided what a submission is before opening it. The barrier follows: where a prior on a source controls admission and corrective evidence from that source is available only downstream of admission, the source cannot correct the prior that excludes it. Evidence may be present, retrievable and even correctly represented while lacking the capacity to alter the decision governing its own admission. And the article's hardest result holds that the criterion favours neither signal: evaluating correctness requires a corpus of established fact, that corpus is itself a source-admission ontology with its own priors, and a source excluded from it cannot correct it — so the barrier recurs, moving from a graph statistic to a curated corpus. Related: #1613, #1626, #1611, #1615.

defines_concepts.definition: The test asked of any representational system: can evidence from a misrepresented object revise the representation that misrepresented it? Where it can, the system can be wrong and find out; where it cannot, it can only be scored. Not a design recommendation, since it asks about the existence of a path rather than about which signal is used.

The recurrence of the source-admission barrier one level up in any content-based trust system: evaluating correctness requires a corpus of established fact, that corpus is itself a source-admission ontology with its own priors, and a source excluded from it cannot correct it. The barrier moves from a graph statistic to a curated corpus rather than dissolving.

Damage to a representation's own capacity to be corrected, as distinct from the two harms already theorized — degradation of ranking quality, studied by adversarial information retrieval, and the wrong done to a discounted speaker, studied by the epistemology of testimony.
